e-8050.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
e-8050.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071806/assets/572d87625c3056d795203d2592c72aa063d1e125d386365ea620b4b596869085.png)

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_i:=R_i+kR_1,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
e-8050.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below $a_{11}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 2 & 2 & -8 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & 10 & -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\qquad$ $R_2:=R_2-2R_1\quad$ and $\quad R_3:=R_3+3R_1.$

e-8048.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
e-8048.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071806/assets/1d7b89b6790ed713a8885b5124d988cda34cccff589ceaef9d556708bc21233f.png)

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- $R_1 := \ldots$

- $R_3:=R_3-3R_2$

- $R_4:= \ldots$

each of the form $R_i:=R_i+kR_2,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
e-8048.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below $a_{22}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\qquad$ $R_1 := R_1 - 2R_2\quad$ and $\quad R_4:=R_4+2R_2.$

e-8051.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
e-8051.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071806/assets/941de9bd4837b4b5c9f0d2bf64c4ea0fd9be657b0368d03cac169742083822d1.png)

By applying elementary column operations of the form $C_i:=C_i+kC_3,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
e-8051.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of $a_{13}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & -5 & 1 \\ 8 & 3 & -4 \\ 9 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+6{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & 1 \\ -16 & 3 & -4 \\ -3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+5{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ -16 & -17 & -4 \\ -3 & -3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\qquad$ $C_1:=C_1+6C_3\quad$ and $\quad C_2:=C_2+5C_3.$

e-8049.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
e-8049.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071806/assets/81176c8bb51128cdaf5d72842e2b2b909b1c41d63249eb3640d745bc9e0c7f9b.png)

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- $C_1:=\ldots$

- $C_3:= C_3 - 4C_2$

- $C_4:= \ldots$

each of the form $C_i:=C_i+kC_2,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
e-8049.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of $a_{32}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -1 & -6 \\ 7 & -2 & -2 & -4 \\ -5 & 1 & 4 & 2 \\ -8 & -3 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+5{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & -1 & -6 \\ -3 & -2 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 2 \\ -23 & -3 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-4{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & 11 & -6 \\ -3 & -2 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -23 & -3 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & 11 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -23 & -3 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\qquad$ $C_1:=C_1+5C_2\quad$ and $\quad C_4:=C_4-2C_2.$

before.html:
Question 1
?

A=[2−413−255−89],B=[2−41−7180−13280]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R2:=R2+5R1 and R3:=R3+9R1
b
R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1
c
R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3+9R1
d
R2:=R2−9R1 and R3:=R3−5R1
e
R2:=R2+5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1
Submit

decision.explanation: Subtracting 5R₁ from R₂ gives (3,-2,5)−5(2,-4,1)=(-7,18,0). Subtracting 9R₁ from R₃ gives (5,-8,9)−9(2,-4,1)=(-13,28,0). These are exactly the rows of B.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}.$

Question 1
?

A=[2−413−255−89],B=[2−41−7180−13280]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R2:=R2+5R1 and R3:=R3+9R1
b
R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1
c
R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3+9R1
d
R2:=R2−9R1 and R3:=R3−5R1
e
R2:=R2+5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make the entries below a13=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[2−413−255−89]R2:=R2−5R1∼[2−41−71805−89]R3:=R3−9R1∼[2−41−7180−13280]=B

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}.$

Question 2
?

A=[−743−122−864],B=[0−10−11−1220−10−12]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1+7R2 and R3:=R3−8R2
b
R1:=R1−8R2 and R3:=R3−7R2
c
R1:=R1−7R2 and R3:=R3+8R2
d
R1:=R1−7R2 and R3:=R3−8R2
e
R1:=R1+7R2 and R3:=R3+8R2
Submit

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -10 & -12\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{21}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-7{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-8{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -10 & -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-7{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-8{R}_{2}.$

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -10 & -12\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{21}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-7{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-8{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -10 & -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-7{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-8{R}_{2}.$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -9 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -6 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -12 & 0 & 21\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{22}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -9 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -6 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -6 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -12 & 0 & 21\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

Question 3
?

A=[3−2−9−3212−6−4−3],B=[003−3212−12021]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1+R2 and R3:=R3−2R2
b
R1:=R1−R2 and R3:=R3−2R2
c
R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3+R2
d
R1:=R1+R2 and R3:=R3+2R2
e
R1:=R1−R2 and R3:=R3+2R2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make the entries above and below a22=2 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[3−2−9−3212−6−4−3]R1:=R1+R2∼[003−3212−6−4−3]R3:=R3+2R2∼[003−3212−12021]=B

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

R1:=R1+R2 and R3:=R3+2R2.

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -9 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -6 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -12 & 0 & 21\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{22}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -9 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -6 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -6 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 12 \\ -12 & 0 & 21\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}.$

A=[4−23−58−7−324],B=[4−231105107]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R2:=R2+R1 and R3:=R3+4R1
b
R2:=R2+4R1 and R3:=R3−R1
c
R2:=R2−4R1 and R3:=R3−R1
d
R2:=R2−4R1 and R3:=R3+R1
e
R2:=R2+4R1 and R3:=R3+R1
Submit

decision.explanation: R₂+4R₁=(-5,8,-7)+4(4,-2,3)=(11,0,5), and R₃+R₁=(-3,2,4)+(4,-2,3)=(1,0,7). These operations produce B exactly.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ -5 & 8 & -7 \\ -3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below ${a}_{12}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ -5 & 8 & -7 \\ -3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 5 \\ -3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}.$

Question 4
?

A=[4−23−58−7−324],B=[4−231105107]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R2:=R2+R1 and R3:=R3+4R1
b
R2:=R2+4R1 and R3:=R3−R1
c
R2:=R2−4R1 and R3:=R3−R1
d
R2:=R2−4R1 and R3:=R3+R1
e
R2:=R2+4R1 and R3:=R3+R1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make the entries below a12=−2 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[4−23−58−7−324]R2:=R2+4R1∼[4−231105−324]R3:=R3+R1∼[4−231105107]=B

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

R2:=R2+4R1 and R3:=R3+R1.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e. R₂+4R₁=(11,0,5) and R₃+R₁=(1,0,7), giving B exactly. Option b incorrectly subtracts R₁ from R₃.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ -5 & 8 & -7 \\ -3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below ${a}_{12}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ -5 & 8 & -7 \\ -3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 5 \\ -3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}.$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 9 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 5 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{33}=-3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 9 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 9 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 5 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}.$

Question 5
?

A=[13325910−3],B=[23055010−3]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1−R3 and R2:=R2−3R3
b
R1:=R1+R3 and R2:=R2+3R3
c
R1:=R1+R3 and R2:=R2−3R3
d
R1:=R1+R3 and R2:=R2+R3
e
R1:=R1−R3 and R2:=R2+3R3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make the entries above a33=−3 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[13325910−3]R1:=R1+R3∼[23025910−3]R2:=R2+3R3∼[23055010−3]=B

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

R1:=R1+R3 and R2:=R2+3R3.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 9 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 5 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{33}=-3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 9 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 9 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 5 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}.$

$$

$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{2}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{32}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 11 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 9 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -7 & -27 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 9 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -7 & -27 \\ 2 & 0 & 7 & 18 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 9 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -7 & -27 \\ 2 & 0 & 7 & 18 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{3}.$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 11 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 9 & 8\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -7 & -27 \\ 2 & 0 & 7 & 18 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{2}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-{R}_{3}$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{32}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 11 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 9 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -7 & -27 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 9 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -7 & -27 \\ 2 & 0 & 7 & 18 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 9 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -7 & -27 \\ 2 & 0 & 7 & 18 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations

after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above ${a}_{42}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 & 14 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ -52 & 0 & -12 & -32 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}

content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above ${a}_{42}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 & 14 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ -52 & 0 & -12 & -32 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{4}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{4}.$

Question 8
?

A=[−85−32246−161−12−10−3−74],B=[−41390246−1109110−213170]

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations

  1. R1:=…
  2. R3:=…
  3. R4:=R4+4R2
each of the form Ri:=Ri+kR2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1+R2 and R3:=R3+R2
b
R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3+2R2
c
R1:=R1−2R2 and R3:=R3+2R2
d
R1:=R1−2R2 and R3:=R3−2R2
e
R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3−2R2
Submit

decision.explanation: R₁+2R₂=(-4,13,9,0) and R₃+2R₂=(10,9,11,0). The given R₄+4R₂=(-2,13,17,0), so these operations produce B exactly.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 5 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ -10 & -3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 13 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 10 & 9 & 11 & 0 \\ -2 & 13 & 17 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+4{R}_{2}$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{24}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & 5 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ -10 & -3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 13 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ -10 & -3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 13 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 10 & 9 & 11 & 0 \\ -10 & -3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 13 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 10 & 9 & 11 & 0 \\ -2 & 13 & 17 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}.$

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations

  1. R1:=…
  2. R3:=…
  3. R4:=R4+4R2
each of the form Ri:=Ri+kR2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1+R2 and R3:=R3+R2
b
R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3+2R2
c
R1:=R1−2R2 and R3:=R3+2R2

R1:=R1−2R2 and R3:=R3−2R2
e
R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3−2R2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries above and below a24=−1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[−85−32246−161−12−10−3−74]R1:=R1+2R2∼[−41390246−161−12−10−3−74]R3:=R3+2R2∼[−41390246−1109110−10−3−74]R4:=R4+4R2∼[−41390246−1109110−213170]=B

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3+2R2.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 5 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ -10 & -3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 13 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 10 & 9 & 11 & 0 \\ -2 & 13 & 17 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+4{R}_{2}$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{24}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & 5 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ -10 & -3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 13 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ -10 & -3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 13 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 10 & 9 & 11 & 0 \\ -10 & -3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 13 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -1 \\ 10 & 9 & 11 & 0 \\ -2 & 13 & 17 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}.$

  1. R2:=…

b

c

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ -7 & 2 & -6 & -7 \\ -8 & 6 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 0 & 12 \\ -18 & -7 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{2}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries below ${a}_{13}=3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ -7 & 2 & -6 & -7 \\ -8 & 6 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ -8 & 6 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 0 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 0 & 12 \\ -18 & -7 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}.$

Submit

EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries below a13=3 equal to 0.

A=[9434−72−6−7−86−380169]R2:=R2+2R1∼[9434111001−86−380169]R3:=R3+R1∼[94341110011100120169]R4:=R4−2R1∼[9434111001110012−18−701]=B

R2:=R2+2R1 and R3:=R3+R1.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option a: R₂+2R₁=(11,10,0,1) and R₃+R₁=(1,10,0,12). Together with R₄−2R₁=(-18,-7,0,1), these give B exactly. Option c incorrectly swaps the multipliers.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ -7 & 2 & -6 & -7 \\ -8 & 6 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 0 & 12 \\ -18 & -7 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{2}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries below ${a}_{13}=3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ -7 & 2 & -6 & -7 \\ -8 & 6 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ -8 & 6 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 0 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 0 & 12 \\ -18 & -7 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}.$

A=[\begin{aligned}-17 & 8 & 0 & 7 \\ -7 & 4 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{2}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{4}$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{4},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above ${a}_{42}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-17 & 8 & 0 & 7 \\ -7 & 4 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ -7 & 4 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{4}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}.$

A=[−17807−74555−45−26−21−1],B=[70435073−70306−21−1]

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations

  1. R1:=…
  2. R2:=…
  3. R3:=R3−2R4
each of the form Ri:=Ri+kR4, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1−4R4 and R2:=R2−2R4
b
R1:=R1+4R4 and R2:=R2−2R4
c
R1:=R1+4R4 and R2:=R2+2R4
d
R1:=R1−4R4 and R2:=R2+2R4
e
R1:=R1+2R4 and R2:=R2+4R4
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries above a42=−2 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[−17807−74555−45−26−21−1]R1:=R1+4R4∼[7043−74555−45−26−21−1]R2:=R2+2R4∼[704350735−45−26−21−1]R3:=R3−2R4∼[70435073−70306−21−1]=B

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

R1:=R1+4R4 and R2:=R2+2R4.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-17 & 8 & 0 & 7 \\ -7 & 4 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{2}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{4}$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{4},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above ${a}_{42}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-17 & 8 & 0 & 7 \\ -7 & 4 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ -7 & 4 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{4}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}.$

Question 11
?

A=[2−143−410209],B=[0−10−5−4−6209]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3−4C2
b
C1:=C1+4C2 and C3:=C3+2C2
c
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3+4C2
d
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3+4C2
e
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−4C2
Submit

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 4 \\ 3 & -4 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ -5 & -4 & -6 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{12}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 4 \\ 3 & -4 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 4 \\ -5 & -4 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ -5 & -4 & -6 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{2}.$

Question 11
?

A=[2−143−410209],B=[0−10−5−4−6209]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3−4C2
b
C1:=C1+4C2 and C3:=C3+2C2
c
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3+4C2
d
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3+4C2
e
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−4C2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the left and to the right of a12=−1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[2−143−410209]C1:=C1+2C2∼[0−14−5−410209]C3:=C3+4C2∼[0−10−5−4−6209]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3+4C2.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 4 \\ 3 & -4 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ -5 & -4 & -6 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{12}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 4 \\ 3 & -4 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 4 \\ -5 & -4 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ -5 & -4 & -6 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{2}.$

before.html:
Question 12
?

A=[−122131341],B=[−7−62−2−11001]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−4C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
b
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2+C3
c
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2−4C3
d
C1:=C1+4C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
e
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2+4C3
Submit

decision.explanation: C₁−3C₃=(-1,1,3)−3(2,1,1)=(-7,-2,0), and C₂−4C₃=(2,3,4)−4(2,1,1)=(-6,-1,0). Keeping C₃ unchanged gives B exactly.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{33}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}.$

A=[−122131341],B=[−7−62−2−11001]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−4C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
b
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2+C3
c
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2−4C3
d
C1:=C1+4C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
e
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2+4C3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the left of a33=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[−122131341]C1:=C1−3C3∼[−722−231041]C2:=C2−4C3∼[−7−62−2−11001]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2−4C3.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option c: C₁−3C₃=(-7,-2,0) and C₂−4C₃=(-6,-1,0), which give B with C₃ unchanged. The submitted option b incorrectly adds C₃ to C₂.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{33}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}.$

Question 13
?

A=[116290119],B=[10027−12103]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C2:=C2−3C1 and C3:=C3−2C1
b
C2:=C2+C1 and C3:=C3−6C1
c
C2:=C2−6C1 and C3:=C3−C1
d
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3+6C1
e
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3−6C1
Submit

decision.explanation: C₂−C₁=(1,9,1)−(1,2,1)=(0,7,0), and C₃−6C₁=(6,0,9)−6(1,2,1)=(0,-12,3). Keeping C₁ unchanged gives B exactly.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & 9 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 7 & -12 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{11}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & 9 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 \\ 2 & 7 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-6{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 7 & -12 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{1}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-6{C}_{1}.$

Question 13
?

A=[116290119],B=[10027−12103]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C2:=C2−3C1 and C3:=C3−2C1
b
C2:=C2+C1 and C3:=C3−6C1
c
C2:=C2−6C1 and C3:=C3−C1
d
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3+6C1
e
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3−6C1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the right of a11=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[116290119]C2:=C2−C1∼[106270109]C3:=C3−6C1∼[10027−12103]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3−6C1.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & 9 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 7 & -12 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{11}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & 9 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 \\ 2 & 7 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-6{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 7 & -12 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{1}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-6{C}_{1}.$

Question 14
?

A=[105−5−13−4880],B=[050−73−1−888]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3+C2
b
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−C2
c
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3+2C2
d
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3+C2
e
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3+C2
Submit

decision.explanation: C₁−2C₂=(10,-1,8)−2(5,3,8)=(0,-7,-8), and C₃+C₂=(-5,-4,0)+(5,3,8)=(0,-1,8). Keeping C₂ unchanged gives B exactly.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}10 & 5 & -5 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 \\ 8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{12}=5$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 5 & -5 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 \\ 8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & -5 \\ -7 & 3 & -4 \\ -8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{2}.$

Question 14
?

A=[105−5−13−4880],B=[050−73−1−888]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3+C2
b
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−C2
c
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3+2C2
d
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3+C2
e
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3+C2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the left and to the right of a12=5 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[105−5−13−4880]C1:=C1−2C2∼[05−5−73−4−880]C3:=C3+C2∼[050−73−1−888]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3+C2.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e: C₁−2C₂=(0,-7,-8) and C₃+C₂=(0,-1,8). Keeping C₂ unchanged produces B exactly. The submitted option b incorrectly subtracts C₂ from C₃.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}10 & 5 & -5 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 \\ 8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{12}=5$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 5 & -5 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 \\ 8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & -5 \\ -7 & 3 & -4 \\ -8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{2}.$

Question 15
?

A=[9−2−16−228042],B=[9720−200042]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3+4C1
b
C2:=C2+4C1 and C3:=C3+C1
c
C2:=C2+C1 and C3:=C3+4C1
d
C2:=C2+C1 and C3:=C3−4C1
e
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3−4C1
Submit

decision.explanation: C₂+C₁=(-2,2,4)+(9,-2,0)=(7,0,4), and C₃+4C₁=(-16,8,2)+4(9,-2,0)=(20,0,2). Keeping C₁ unchanged gives B exactly.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 & -16 \\ -2 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}9 & 7 & 20 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 & -16 \\ -2 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 7 & -16 \\ -2 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 7 & 20 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+{C}_{1}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{1}.$

Question 15
?

A=[9−2−16−228042],B=[9720−200042]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3+4C1
b
C2:=C2+4C1 and C3:=C3+C1
c
C2:=C2+C1 and C3:=C3+4C1
d
C2:=C2+C1 and C3:=C3−4C1
e
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3−4C1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the right of a21=−2 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[9−2−16−228042]C2:=C2+C1∼[97−16−208042]C3:=C3+4C1∼[9720−200042]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C2:=C2+C1 and C3:=C3+4C1.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 & -16 \\ -2 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}9 & 7 & 20 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 & -16 \\ -2 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 7 & -16 \\ -2 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 7 & 20 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+{C}_{1}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{1}.$

Question 16
?

A=[−1223131−2314−24−2−3−4],B=[−3−4270010−1−114677−3−10]

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

  1. C1:=…
  2. C2:=…
  3. C4:=C4+2C3
each of the form Ci:=Ci+kC3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2−C3
b
C1:=C1−C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
c
C1:=C1+C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
d
C1:=C1−C3 and C2:=C2−C3
e
C1:=C1−C3 and C2:=C2+3C3
Submit

decision.explanation: C₁−C₃=(-3,0,-1,7), and C₂−3C₃=(-4,0,-11,7). Together with the given C₄+2C₃=(7,0,6,-10), these produce B exactly.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -11 & 4 & 6 \\ 7 & 7 & -3 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{3}$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{23}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 7 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -11 & 4 & -2 \\ 7 & 7 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -11 & 4 & 6 \\ 7 & 7 & -3 & -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-3{C}_{3}.$

$$

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-3{C}_{3}.$

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

  1. C2:=…

decision.explanation: C₂−4C₁=(0,0,3,3), and C₄+3C₁=(4,0,2,-2). Together with the given C₃−5C₁=(-4,0,7,1), these produce B exactly.

after.name: Question 17
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 & -3 \\ -2 & -5 & -3 & 8 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 7 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-5{C}_{1}$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 & -3 \\ -2 & -5 & -3 & 8 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 & 8 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-5{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & 7 & 8 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 7 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{1}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{1}.$

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

  1. C2:=…
  2. C3:=C3−5C1
  3. C4:=…
each of the form Ci:=Ci+kC1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary column operations?

a
C2:=C2−2C1 and C4:=C4+3C1
b
C2:=C2−3C1 and C4:=C4+4C1
c
C2:=C2−4C1 and C4:=C4−3C1
d
C2:=C2+4C1 and C4:=C4+3C1
e
C2:=C2−4C1 and C4:=C4+3C1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the right of a21=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[286−2145−3−2−5−38−1−1−41]C2:=C2−4C1∼[206−2105−3−23−38−13−41]C3:=C3−5C1∼[20−4−2100−3−2378−1311]C4:=C4+3C1∼[20−441000−2372−131−2]=B.

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

C2:=C2−4C1 and C4:=C4+3C1.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e: C₂−4C₁=(0,0,3,3) and C₄+3C₁=(4,0,2,-2). Together with the given C₃−5C₁=(-4,0,7,1), these produce B exactly. Option a uses an incorrect multiplier for C₂.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 & -3 \\ -2 & -5 & -3 & 8 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 7 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-5{C}_{1}$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 & -3 \\ -2 & -5 & -3 & 8 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 & 8 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-5{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & 7 & 8 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 7 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{1}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{1}.$

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

  1. C1:=C1−4C4
  2. C2:=…
  3. C3:=…
each of the form Ci:=Ci+kC4, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary column operations?

a
C2:=C2−5C4 and C3:=C3−3C4
b
C2:=C2−3C4 and C3:=C3−5C4
c
C2:=C2+5C4 and C3:=C3+3C4

Submit

decision.explanation: C₂−5C₄=(1,1,9,5)−5(1,5,4,1)=(-4,-24,-11,0), and C₃−3C₄=(6,2,-5,3)−3(1,5,4,1)=(3,-13,-17,0). Together with the given operation on C₁, these produce B exactly.

after.name: Question 18
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 8 & 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -12 & -24 & -13 & 5 \\ -16 & -11 & -17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{4}$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{3}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{4},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{44}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 8 & 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ -12 & 1 & 2 & 5 \\ -16 & 9 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-5{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 6 & 1 \\ -12 & -24 & 2 & 5 \\ -16 & -11 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -12 & -24 & -13 & 5 \\ -16 & -11 & -17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-5{C}_{4}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{4}.$

  1. C1:=C1−4C4

A=[1161812509−544531]C1:=C1−4C4∼[−3161−12125−169−540531]C2:=C2−5C4∼[−3−461−12−2425−16−11−540031]C3:=C3−3C4∼[−3−431−12−24−135−16−11−1740001]=B.

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

C2:=C2−5C4 and C3:=C3−3C4.

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 8 & 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -12 & -24 & -13 & 5 \\ -16 & -11 & -17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{4}$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{3}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{4},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{44}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 8 & 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ -12 & 1 & 2 & 5 \\ -16 & 9 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-5{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 6 & 1 \\ -12 & -24 & 2 & 5 \\ -16 & -11 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -12 & -24 & -13 & 5 \\ -16 & -11 & -17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-5{C}_{4}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{4}.$

Question 19
?

A=[212308046913−6−11−6],B=[0100−168−16−20−129−17−24−4−13−3]

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

  1. C1:=…
  2. C3:=…
  3. C4:=C4−3C2
each of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−2C2
b
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−3C2
c
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3−C2
d
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3+2C2
e
C1:=C1+C2 and C3:=C3+C2
Submit

decision.explanation: C₁−2C₂=(0,-16,-12,-4), and C₃−2C₂=(0,-16,-17,3). Together with the given C₄−3C₂=(0,-20,-24,-3), these produce B exactly.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 & 4 \\ 6 & 9 & 1 & 3 \\ -6 & -1 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -16 & 8 & -16 & -20 \\ -12 & 9 & -17 & -24 \\ -4 & -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{3}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-3{C}_{2}$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{12}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 & 4 \\ 6 & 9 & 1 & 3 \\ -6 & -1 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -16 & 8 & 0 & 4 \\ -12 & 9 & 1 & 3 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -16 & 8 & -16 & 4 \\ -12 & 9 & -17 & 3 \\ -4 & -1 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -16 & 8 & -16 & -20 \\ -12 & 9 & -17 & -24 \\ -4 & -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-2{C}_{2}.$

Question 19
?

A=[212308046913−6−11−6],B=[0100−168−16−20−129−17−24−4−13−3]

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

  1. C1:=…
  2. C3:=…
  3. C4:=C4−3C2
each of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−2C2
b
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−3C2
c
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3−C2
d
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3+2C2
e
C1:=C1+C2 and C3:=C3+C2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the left and to the right of a12=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[212308046913−6−11−6]C1:=C1−2C2∼[0123−16804−12913−4−11−6]C3:=C3−2C2∼[0103−168−164−129−173−4−13−6]C4:=C4−3C2∼[0100−168−16−20−129−17−24−4−13−3]=B.

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−2C2.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option a: C₁−2C₂=(0,-16,-12,-4) and C₃−2C₂=(0,-16,-17,3). Together with C₄−3C₂=(0,-20,-24,-3), these produce B exactly. Option b uses the wrong multiplier for C₃.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 & 4 \\ 6 & 9 & 1 & 3 \\ -6 & -1 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -16 & 8 & -16 & -20 \\ -12 & 9 & -17 & -24 \\ -4 & -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{3}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-3{C}_{2}$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{12}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 & 4 \\ 6 & 9 & 1 & 3 \\ -6 & -1 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -16 & 8 & 0 & 4 \\ -12 & 9 & 1 & 3 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -16 & 8 & -16 & 4 \\ -12 & 9 & -17 & 3 \\ -4 & -1 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -16 & 8 & -16 & -20 \\ -12 & 9 & -17 & -24 \\ -4 & -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-2{C}_{2}.$

decision.explanation: C₃+3C₂=(0,4,3,4)+3(0,2,-1,0)=(0,10,0,4), and C₄−2C₂=(7,8,-2,1)−2(0,2,-1,0)=(7,4,0,1). Together with the given operation on C₁, these produce B exactly.

after.name: Question 20
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ -8 & 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 10 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+5{C}_{2}$
- ${C}_{3}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ -8 & 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+5{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 10 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 10 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}.$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ -8 & 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 10 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+5{C}_{2}$
- ${C}_{3}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ -8 & 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+5{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 10 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 10 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}.$
